The service, called Truth PSI, was announced Thursday by Trump Media & Technology Group.

San Francisco’s city attorney is urging a state court to block Trump’s social media platform Truth Social from offering customers who pay $100,000 per month priority access to the president’s and other high-level officials’ posts before they’re available to other users.
The lawsuit comes on the heels of a similar one filed in federal court last week where two nonprofits challenged the constitutionality of the paid service called “Truth API.”

Providing early access to subscribers of “announcements of consequential government decisions that can move financial markets” would create “a financial gain for Trump Media,” as well as for President Donald Trump , who owns 41% of Trump Media through a revocable trust in which he is the sole beneficiary, the lawsuit said.

“Truth API disadvantages regular investors, including individuals who hold investments via pension funds, 401(k) plans, and other retirement funds, whose investment vehicles do not and/or cannot obtain Truth API’s early-access information,” the complaint said.

On Monday a group of former prosecutors and federal agents filed an amicus brief in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York arguing the paid subscription could violate federal securities laws, the Trade Secrets Act, and could constitute illegal outside compensation for federal employment.
The case is California v. Trump Media & Tech Grp. , Cal. Super. Ct., complaint filed 9/21/26.
